_meta.status: energy and fixed rates verified from NEPRA PDF via research; add-ons below are secondary sources and must be re-checked monthly
_meta.rules: Protected: benefit of one previous slab. Unprotected: all units at the rate of the band reached. Fixed charge = Rs/kW/month x sanctioned kW. >=5 kW must be ToU.

tou.fixed_basis: higher of 50% sanctioned load or MDI

peak_hours.applies_to: ex-WAPDA DISCOs (LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO, GEPCO, FESCO, PESCO, HESCO, SEPCO, QESCO, TESCO), consumers on a Time-of-Use meter (5 kW or more sanctioned load); every other hour is off-peak
peak_hours.source: NEPRA tariff determination for IESCO FY2023-24 (schedule of peak and off-peak timings for ToU tariffs); the December to February window is also published by PITC's bill portal
peak_hours.note: Latest NEPRA schedule found is dated 2023; an August 2025 news report says NEPRA asked DISCOs to propose peak hours up to 11 pm only, adoption not confirmed. K-Electric publishes its own timings. Re-check against the current DISCO tariff schedule.

fc_surcharge_per_unit.by_category_note: Default per consumer category when the page field is blank (engine/bill.js addOns, audit 2026-10-21 WL-241, WL-243). Lifeline: no FC surcharge, from NEPRA's category table. Protected: 0 by default [VERIFY, WL-242/243]: no NEPRA or Power Division notification found that sets the protected rate for 2026. NEPRA's 2023 decision raised the surcharge to Rs 3.23 for every category except protected domestic consumers (news reports only; the protected rate was then reported as lower, Rs 0.43 or Rs 1.43). A LESCO protected bill (September 2026) is evidence only, not the source (owner rule 21 Oct 2026: a bill can carry over-billing): its total reconciles with FC 0 and with no other rate. Replace with the primary notification when found.
fc_surcharge_per_unit.by_category_source: NEPRA decision on the Financing Cost (FC) surcharge for ex-WAPDA DISCOs, TRF-100, 6 March 2023: consumer category table, lifeline row without the surcharge (primary). Protected: no primary source yet; Business Recorder 40230809 and Dawn 1741521 (2023, secondary) on the Rs 3.23 surcharge excluding protected consumers; a LESCO protected bill for September 2026 as evidence (checked 30 October 2026).

qta_per_unit.verified_note: Per quarter in sources: 2026-03..2026-05 and 2026-09..2026-11 from NEPRA's notifications (primary, protected homes included); 2026-06..2026-08 still from news reports.

2026-03..2026-05.source: NEPRA notification SRO 459(I)/2026, quarterly adjustment for the 2nd quarter FY 2025-26: uniform Rs 0.3504/kWh, March to May 2026, all consumer categories except lifeline, incremental package units and prepaid

2026-06..2026-08.source: news reports of NEPRA's quarterly adjustment (Rs 1.98 to 1.99 per unit cut, June 2026); NEPRA notification not found

2026-09..2026-11.source: NEPRA notification SRO 1501(I)/2026 (7 September 2026), quarterly adjustment for the 2nd quarter CY 2026: uniform Rs 0.5194/kWh, September to November 2026, all consumer categories except lifeline, incremental package units and prepaid (also K-Electric)

fpa_per_unit.note: Changes monthly. The monthly FPA history lives only in data/bill-index.json (months[].fpa_per_unit); pages that explain the FPA and the bill calculators F1 to F12 pre-fill its newest NEPRA-verified month (build: data.fpa_latest; audit WL-13, WL-229), every other caller leaves it at 0 when blank. NEPRA's FCA orders charge it to every consumer category except lifeline, EV charging stations and prepaid (July 2026 order para 21(a); March 2026 notification para 4(a)). The March 2026 review decision (SRO 852(I)/2026) added protected consumers for that one month only (a negative FCA), so it is not a standing exemption (audit WL-157).
fpa_per_unit.exempt_note: Consumer categories the bill engine does not charge the FPA (engine/bill.js addOns). Only lifeline among the categories the engine models; EV charging stations and prepaid consumers are also exempt, but the calculators do not model them. A data/bill-index.json month can carry its own list (fpa_exempt) when an order differs.
fpa_per_unit.exempt_source: NEPRA decision on the fuel charges adjustment for July 2026, SRO 1499(I)/2026, para 21(a): applicable to all consumer categories of K-Electric and ex-WAPDA DISCOs except lifeline consumers, EVCS and prepaid consumers (checked 2026-10-21): https://nepra.org.pk/tariff/Tariff/Ex-WAPDA%20DISCOS/2026/TRF-100%20MFPA%20FOR%20THE%20MONTH%20OF%20JULY%202026%20EX-WAPDA%20DISCOS%2004-09-2026%2018342-60.PDF
fpa_per_unit.range_note: Input bound only (audit WL-118): a sanity range wider than any monthly FCA NEPRA has notified for domestic consumers (the largest, Rs 9.90 per unit for June 2022, was charged in August 2022 bills). A value outside it is almost certainly a typing mistake (for example the bill's FPA amount in rupees instead of the rate per unit). Widen it if NEPRA ever notifies a larger adjustment.
fpa_per_unit.range_source: Dawn, 'Nepra approves Rs9.90 per unit fuel price hike' (July 2022); secondary

income_tax_235.applies_to: domestic consumers not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List (ATL); monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more
income_tax_235.note: Advance income tax on electricity bills, Income Tax Ordinance 2001 section 235 (domestic consumers brought in by the Finance Act 2021). Not added by the bill engine because it depends on the consumer's tax status; pages mention it (audit WL-14c, WL-49). Confirm against the current FBR withholding tax card at each budget.
income_tax_235.source: PkRevenue: 'Domestic electricity consumers to pay tax on monthly bill above Rs25,000' and 'Electricity withholding tax not applicable on ATL domestic consumers' (FBR withholding rates); secondary

gst_pct.by_category_note: Lifeline GST stays 0 by default, as before, until the owner's expert or a real lifeline bill confirms it [VERIFY, WL-241]. No FBR exemption for lifeline was found; secondary sources say lifeline bills pay GST (a 2012 ministry statement put the GST exemption at 1 to 50 units only). The user can still enter GST on the page. Protected: the full value. Source: the Sales Tax Act 1990, section 3(1) standard rate of 18% on the value of supply, which includes the FPA; no exemption for protected domestic consumers was found. A LESCO protected bill (September 2026) is consistent with it (evidence only, not the source).
gst_pct.by_category_source: Business Recorder report 3974034 and a FESCO consumer guide (secondary); no primary FBR source found.

ptv_fee.note: removal announced 29 Jun 2025; effective date unconfirmed

net_billing.buyback_basis: Regulation 14(1)(b): units a prosumer exports are billed at the national average energy purchase price (NAEPP). Regulation 14(3): NEPRA may revise the rate by notification.
net_billing.buyback_source: NEPRA decision on the Power Purchase Price forecast for CY 2026 (7 Jan 2026), para 36: NAEPP Rs 8.13/kWh, NAPPP Rs 25.32/kWh
net_billing.existing_prosumers: Agreements signed before 9 Feb 2026 stay on the rate and mechanism of the repealed 2015 net-metering regulations until they expire (SRO 547(I)/2026, 2 Apr 2026, substitutes regulation 21(2), deemed effective 9 Feb 2026; the first version had set them at the national average power purchase price). A material modification that changes the maximum output (e.g. adding panels) ends those terms early. Renewals move to net billing (regulation 21(3)).
net_billing.note: Size capped at sanctioned load. NAEPP is set for each calendar year in NEPRA's power purchase price decision; re-check every January and when NEPRA notifies a revision. Kept editable for a DISCO that applies a revised rate.
net_billing.reported_source: Express Tribune, 10 Feb 2026: news report of a buyback of about Rs 11 a unit under discussion; not notified by NEPRA. Shown only to explain the figure news and other sites quote; the calculator default stays the NEPRA NAEPP above (audit WL-248).

discos_note: The DISCO select on D10 (net billing review 30 Oct 2026, WL-251). Every DISCO here bills A-1 domestic consumers on the same uniform slab rates, so the choice only names the company in the result and the shared text; it changes no number. Key = the name printed on the bill, value = the head office city shown in the list.
discos_source: NEPRA tariff rationalization decision for ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric, 11 Feb 2026 (source_url at the top of this file): one A-1 schedule for the ten ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric
